document.title: Teach System Diagram four explanatory grammars without changing its style
document.summary: PRD and Design Solution decide when and what a situation needs to illustrate; System Diagram generates sequence, flow, architecture, or component diagrams in the established infrastructure visual language without inventing meaning.
document.reviewFocus: Confirm that capability selection, authority boundaries, staged delivery, sequence limits, and observable acceptance fully express the approved direction; then explicitly approve or request changes to the complete PRD.
sources: Explicit approvals from Carlos Rodrigo in the 2026-08-03 conversation: extend the existing System Diagram skill, keep its current style, adopt sequence/flow/architecture/component capabilities, use sequence first, accept the proposed limits, and preserve the PRD/Design/System Diagram responsibility split.

sections.title: Owning document skills can request the right explanatory figure
sections.summary: The product change expands one existing skill rather than creating competing diagram tools or styles.

blocks.text: For a PRD or Design Solution that needs to explain an evidence-backed situation during document review, the product will generate the appropriate sequence, flow, architecture, or component diagram through the existing System Diagram skill, resulting in a deterministic figure that a reviewer can retell; it will not transfer product or architecture authority to the renderer or introduce another visual language.

items: Approved product truth
Carlos Rodrigo approved this capability and ownership direction in the 2026-08-03 conversation.
Actor
PRD or Design Solution composing a durable review document
Moment
A sourced product or architecture situation needs a causal, temporal, topological, or decomposition explanation
Entry
A bounded semantic brief containing the question, audience, evidence, scope, path, uncertainty, and walkthrough
Result
One validated, accessible, style-consistent diagram and retained regeneration source
Boundary
System Diagram validates and renders supplied meaning; it does not decide what the product or architecture means

sections.title: One generic graph contract cannot teach every requested situation
sections.summary: The current skill is dependable but its source model is limited to manually positioned generic graph elements.

items: Sourced fact
skills/system-diagram/scripts/diagram-spec.mjs accepts rectangular nodes, groups, and explicitly routed orthogonal edges.
Sourced fact
skills/system-diagram/references/diagram-modes.md classifies semantic questions but does not define participant lifelines, flow decisions/merges, architecture levels, or component interfaces.
Consequence
Temporal interaction must be approximated as a generic graph, while flow, architecture, and component authors must manually recreate conventions that the skill should know.

blocks.title: Plausible drawing is not enough
blocks.text: Without typed semantics and selection guidance, a diagram may look consistent while answering the wrong question or implying unsupported product or architecture truth.

sections.title: The owning skill chooses the question; System Diagram generates the explanation
sections.summary: Approved product truth — Carlos Rodrigo approved that selection follows the situation being explained, while domain authority remains with PRD or Design Solution.

items.title: Own the situation
items.text: PRD or Design Solution states the question, evidence, scope, main path, uncertainty, and product or architecture meaning.

items.title: Select the capability
items.text: The owning skill chooses sequence for temporal communication, flow for progression and branching, architecture for static bounded communication, or component for decomposition of one scope.

items.title: Validate the brief
items.text: System Diagram rejects missing evidence, unsupported semantics, invalid references, excessive complexity, or a brief that needs splitting.

items.title: Generate in one style
items.text: System Diagram applies the selected grammar and emits deterministic source/SVG using the existing infrastructure-v1 language.

items.title: Embed without reinterpretation
items.text: HTML Report Designer verifies provenance and embeds the figure with the owning document's walkthrough.

items: PRD uses diagrams to explain actor-visible product behavior and never introduces architecture.
Design Solution uses diagrams to explain approved boundaries, state, communication, recovery, or decomposition.
System Diagram owns generation mechanics and the established style, never product or architecture truth.
HTML Report Designer validates and embeds; it does not choose a capability or redraw the figure.
Existing system-diagram-v1 sources and generated SVGs remain valid and visually unchanged.
Unsupported or crowded meaning returns an actionable blocker instead of a plausible approximation or smaller text.

sections.title: Authority stays with the document while generation becomes capability-aware
sections.summary: Approved product truth — the owning document supplies meaning, System Diagram validates and generates, and unsupported meaning returns for refinement.

blocks.question: How does an owning document skill turn an evidence-backed situation into the right style-consistent diagram without transferring product or architecture authority?
blocks.caption: PRD or Design Solution supplies and owns meaning; System Diagram validates one selected grammar and renders it in the established style; unsupported briefs return for refinement.
walkthrough: PRD or Design Solution identifies a situation that needs explanation and owns its product or architecture meaning.
The owning skill supplies a bounded evidence-backed brief and selects sequence, flow, architecture, or component from the explanatory question.
System Diagram validates evidence, semantics, limits, and uncertainty without adding unsupported truth.
Supported meaning becomes deterministic infrastructure-v1 SVG; ambiguous or excessive meaning returns for refinement or splitting.
HTML Report Designer verifies and embeds the figure so the reviewer can retell the situation.

sections.title: Five end-to-end outcomes expand the skill safely
sections.summary: Approved product truth — sequence, flow, architecture view, and component decomposition are staged capabilities of the same System Diagram skill and visual language.

blocks.title: Choose the capability from the explanatory question
blocks.outcome: PRD or Design Solution can request a diagram that matches the situation being reviewed.
blocks.boundary: System Diagram does not infer product or architecture truth, and capability choice does not authorize additional diagrams or implementation.

story.capability: select an explanatory diagram capability from a bounded situation
story.outcome: the generated figure answers the intended question without changing its meaning

scenarios.title: Supported explanatory question
scenarios.given: PRD or Design Solution has a sourced situation, audience, question, path, uncertainty, and walkthrough
scenarios.when: it classifies the question as temporal communication, progression, bounded topology, or one-scope decomposition
scenarios.then: it hands System Diagram one sequence, flow, architecture, or component brief with the original authority intact

scenarios.title: Ambiguous or unsupported question
scenarios.given: the brief mixes incompatible abstraction levels, lacks evidence, or cannot identify one explanatory question
scenarios.then: it returns a blocker asking the owning skill to clarify or split the situation instead of drawing a plausible figure

steps.title: Classify and hand off
steps.context: The owning document has one evidence-backed situation to explain.
steps.action: It matches the question to one capability and supplies the semantic brief.
steps.response: System Diagram accepts a bounded request or returns the exact missing condition.
steps.outcome: Only supported meaning advances to generation.

acceptance.text: Selection guidance distinguishes temporal communication, progression/branching, static bounded communication, and one-scope decomposition with no overlapping default.
A brief with missing evidence, mixed abstraction, or unsupported semantics produces a blocker that identifies what must be clarified or split.
Generated labels, actors, states, boundaries, and relationships all trace to the owning brief rather than renderer inference.

blocks.after: After this slice, the document workflow can choose one explanatory capability without transferring semantic authority.

blocks.title: Explain temporal communication with a sequence diagram
blocks.outcome: A reviewer can follow who communicates with whom and in what order, including material alternatives or recovery.
blocks.boundary: The initial capability excludes timing diagrams, actor creation/destruction, arbitrary icons, and deeply nested parallel or critical fragments.

story.actor: a PRD or Design Solution author
story.capability: explain participant communication in temporal order
story.outcome: the reviewer can follow the interaction and its recovery without reading a generic graph

scenarios.title: Temporal interaction
scenarios.given: the brief names ordered participants, messages, material notes, activation spans, and any alternative, optional, or loop fragment
scenarios.when: System Diagram generates the sequence capability
scenarios.then: the figure preserves participant and event order through lifelines, labelled messages, explicit fragments, and the existing visual language

scenarios.title: Sequence exceeds the approved envelope
scenarios.given: the brief exceeds an approved participant, event, nesting, activation, text, or output limit
scenarios.then: generation stops and asks the owning skill to split the interaction rather than compress or omit meaning

steps.title: Order the interaction
steps.context: A supported temporal brief is complete and source ordered.
steps.action: System Diagram maps participants, events, activations, and fragments to the sequence grammar.
steps.response: A deterministic lifeline figure preserves the approved order and style.
steps.outcome: The reviewer can narrate the normal and recovery interaction.

acceptance.text: Sequence output preserves one to eight participants and one to forty-eight messages in source order, with no more than sixty-four total events.
The capability represents synchronous, asynchronous, return, and self messages plus notes, explicit activations, and bounded alt, opt, and loop fragments when supplied.
The approved envelope allows at most sixteen notes, twelve fragments at depth three, and sixteen activations at simultaneous depth three; exceeding it fails with split guidance.
Sequence output uses the established infrastructure-v1 visual language and does not change byte-current v1 fixtures.

blocks.after: After this slice, System Diagram can generate its first genuinely temporal explanatory figure.

blocks.title: Explain progression and recovery with a flow diagram
blocks.outcome: A reviewer can follow work or state from trigger through decisions to outcome or recovery.
blocks.boundary: The flow is not an architecture inventory and does not use page composition to explain causality.

story.actor: a product or architecture document author
story.capability: explain progression, branching, and recovery as one flow
story.outcome: the reviewer can identify each guarded decision and resulting outcome

scenarios.title: Bounded progression
scenarios.given: the brief supplies a start, ordered actions or states, guarded decisions, merges, outcomes, and material feedback or recovery
scenarios.when: System Diagram generates the flow capability
scenarios.then: the figure presents one readable progression with labelled branches and explicit outcome or recovery paths

steps.title: Trace the progression
steps.context: The brief asks how work or state advances rather than what systems exist.
steps.action: System Diagram arranges supplied actions and guarded branches in causal order.
steps.response: The generated flow keeps the main path and material recovery distinguishable.
steps.outcome: The reviewer can explain how each outcome is reached.

acceptance.text: Every decision has labelled outgoing meaning, and each accepted element lies on a path from the supplied start to an outcome or recovery.
A disconnected element, unlabeled decision branch, or unsupported loop fails instead of appearing as unexplained adjacency.
The flow remains readable in the established style at desktop, local 320px overflow, and print sizes.

blocks.after: After this slice, System Diagram can generate bounded causal flows without treating a generic node map as a process.

blocks.title: Explain bounded communication with an architecture view
blocks.outcome: A reviewer can see which systems or containers communicate across relevant runtime or ownership boundaries.
blocks.boundary: One figure uses one declared abstraction level; deployment instances, automatic multi-level zoom, and vendor icon packs remain out of scope.

story.capability: explain static communication at one architecture level
story.outcome: the reviewer can identify responsibilities, boundaries, and labelled relationships

scenarios.title: One bounded architecture level
scenarios.given: the approved design brief names one context or container scope, relevant people or runtime units, boundaries, and labelled relationships
scenarios.when: System Diagram generates the architecture capability
scenarios.then: the figure preserves the declared level and makes every material boundary crossing explicit

steps.title: Map one architecture level
steps.context: Design Solution supplies approved static topology and relevant boundaries.
steps.action: System Diagram places the units and their labelled directional relationships within that scope.
steps.response: The architecture view exposes communication without mixing context, container, component, or deployment levels.
steps.outcome: The reviewer can retell the bounded topology.

acceptance.text: Architecture output declares one context or container level and rejects invalid nesting or mixed abstraction.
Every relationship is directional and labelled, and a runtime/container boundary crossing includes the supplied protocol.
PRD cannot use the architecture capability to introduce technical boundaries that are absent from approved product truth.

blocks.after: After this slice, Design Solution can request a consistent static architecture explanation without changing diagram style.

blocks.title: Explain one scope through component decomposition
blocks.outcome: A reviewer can understand how one approved container or module decomposes and which interfaces connect its parts.
blocks.boundary: The capability does not produce class/member diagrams, source-file inventories, or whole-system deployment views.

story.capability: explain component responsibilities and interfaces inside one scope
story.outcome: the reviewer can identify each dependency and unresolved contract

scenarios.title: One-scope decomposition
scenarios.given: the approved design brief names one container or module, its components, short responsibilities, interfaces, and dependencies
scenarios.when: System Diagram generates the component capability
scenarios.then: the figure shows the internal decomposition and rejects required interfaces that have no supplied provider

steps.title: Decompose one scope
steps.context: Design Solution supplies one bounded container or module and its approved contracts.
steps.action: System Diagram maps components, provided and required interfaces, and dependencies.
steps.response: The generated component view exposes matched contracts and blocks unresolved required interfaces.
steps.outcome: The reviewer can explain how the scope is internally connected.

acceptance.text: Component output contains exactly one container or module scope and gives each component a supplied responsibility.
Every interface has unique supplied ownership, every dependency resolves to existing elements, and unmatched required interfaces fail validation.
The output omits classes, members, source files, and unrelated external topology.

blocks.after: After this slice, Design Solution can explain one component boundary without turning the diagram into a code inventory.

sections.title: One skill and one visual language, delivered in bounded slices

items: Approved product truth
Carlos Rodrigo approved extending the existing System Diagram skill, preserving infrastructure-v1, using sequence first, and keeping semantic authority with PRD and Design Solution.
In
Capability-selection guidance, sequence/flow/architecture/component generation, deterministic retained source/SVG, accessibility, report embedding, failure guidance, and behavioral evaluation.
Sequence capacity
Up to 8 participants, 48 messages, 64 events, 16 notes, 12 fragments at depth 3, and 16 activations at simultaneous depth 3.
Design input
The approved research also fixes raw-source, text, geometry, output-size, one-pass layout, Node 18, and byte-compatibility guardrails for technical design.
Out
A new visual language, a universal graph engine before evidence, page composition, class diagrams, automatic semantic invention, generic migration, or implementation tasks before design approval.
Mockups
Not applicable — this feature changes generated explanatory artifacts, not an interactive interface or responsive page composition, and retains the already approved visual style.

sections.title: Capability, authority, and delivery direction are explicit

blocks.question: How should the four diagram capabilities enter the workflow?

options.label: Extend the existing System Diagram skill and reuse infrastructure-v1
Create separate diagram skills or visual languages for each type

blocks.rationale: One skill can learn multiple explanatory grammars while preserving the visual and validation contract reviewers already recognize.

blocks.question: Who decides when, what, and how a situation is illustrated?

options.label: PRD/Design Solution own when and what; System Diagram owns generation; HTML Report Designer embeds
System Diagram infers the situation and report placement from available files

blocks.rationale: Product and architecture authority must remain with the skills that own those domains; rendering cannot safely invent semantics.

blocks.question: How should implementation progress across the four capabilities?

options.label: Deliver sequence as the first complete vertical slice, then evaluate each graph capability
Build shared foundations for all four capabilities before one works end to end

blocks.rationale: Sequence is the genuinely new temporal grammar; a complete slice proves the contract before shared abstractions or additional graph behavior are justified.
